shipped_row.boundary_rationale: An explicit quotative frame opens this short strophe: אַחַ֗ת הִ֥יא עַל כֵּ֥ן (glossed ‘it is all one; therefore I say’, Job.9.22), introducing the indictment “he destroys the blameless and the wicked” web:Job.9.22. This opening word, תָּ֥ם (‘blameless’), repeats — at byte tier — the word that twice closes the preceding strophe's argument (תָּֽם at Job.9.20 word 5, תָּֽם at Job.9.21 word 1), a cross-seam lexical bond disclosed here rather than left implicit; it corroborates continuity of the courtroom-to-indictment argument across 9.21|9.22 without moving either strophe's edge. Job.9.23-Job.9.24 extend the same indictment: Job.9.22's מְכַלֶּֽה (‘destroys’) carries an explicit third-person subject, ה֣וּא, and Job.9.23's נְקִיִּ֣ם (‘mocks’) has no expressed subject of its own — WEB's own rendering keeps the pronoun 'he' across the verse boundary rather than naming 'the scourge' as a fresh subject, so the mocking agent is left as open a question in the Hebrew as in English; either way the indictment stays continuous, reaching “The earth is given into the hand of the wicked” web:Job.9.24, closing on the rhetorical question “If not he, then who is it?” web:Job.9.24. The subject shifts from this cosmic indictment to Job's own fleeting days at Job.9.25, marking the strophe's far edge.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding Job.9.22-Job.9.24 into the preceding courtroom-inability argument was rejected given the explicit inferential frame that opens Job.9.22 and the fresh third-person subject (earth, judges) it introduces.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: theodicy indictment: God mocks the calamity of innocent

prev_row.boundary_rationale: An a-fortiori particle opens the strophe: אַ֭ף כִּֽי (glossed ‘how much less’, Job.9.14), drawing the direct implication from the preceding power-hymn that Job himself cannot answer God. A chain of אם-protases follows (Job.9.15-Job.9.16, Job.9.19-Job.9.20) arguing that no hearing could be fair even for an innocent man: “Though I am righteous, my own mouth will condemn me” web:Job.9.20. The strophe closes on the bare declarative תָּֽם אָ֭נִי (“I am blameless. I don't respect myself. I despise my life.” web:Job.9.21), a personal verdict that ends the courtroom-inability argument before the inferential turn of Job.9.22.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Closing this strophe at Job.9.20 was rejected because Job.9.21's self-verdict completes the courtroom argument's clause chain rather than opening an unrelated one.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: complaint of innocence: all alike perish by divine hand

next_row.boundary_rationale: The fronted possessive subject וְיָמַ֣י קַ֭לּוּ (“Now my days are swifter than a runner” web:Job.9.25) turns the topic from the theodicy indictment to Job's own vanishing lifespan, using simile (“as the swift ships, as the eagle that swoops on the prey” web:Job.9.26). A pair of אם-protases then brackets the futility of self-vindication: Job.9.27 ( “I will forget my complaint” web:Job.9.27 ) and Job.9.30 ( washing with snow ), both resolving to the same fear ( “I know that you will not hold me innocent” web:Job.9.28 ) and closing on “My own clothes will abhor me” web:Job.9.31, before the כי-clause of Job.9.32 reopens the courtroom register directly.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A break at Job.9.27|Job.9.28 was considered but rejected since the paired אם-protases of Job.9.27 and Job.9.30 frame one continuous argument about the futility of self-cleansing.
next_row.literature_type_guess: fleeting days complaint: life flies like courier and shuttle

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: The strophe turns from the oppression-themed interrogatives to creation imagery with a fronted address: יָדֶ֣יךָ עִ֭צְּבוּנִי, “Your hands have framed me and fashioned me altogether, yet you destroy me.” web:Job.10.8 — the same verse that opens the strophe on gift-language closes on the identical undoing threatened at the strophe's far edge. Job.10.9 asks “Will you bring me into dust again?” web:Job.10.9, a second reminder that the creation imagery already carries its own destruction inside this strophe, not just across the seam at Job.10.13. The imagery continues through the positive acts of formation, “clothed me with skin and flesh” web:Job.10.11, and closes on “Your visitation has preserved my spirit” web:Job.10.12, before the adversative pivot of Job.10.13 makes explicit, through a fronted demonstrative object not used earlier in the strophe, the hostility that Job.10.8-Job.10.9 have already voiced twice in passing.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging Job.10.8-Job.10.12 with the accusation that follows was rejected because the adversative fronting at Job.10.13 — not merely destructive content, which already appears in passing at Job.10.8-Job.10.9 — marks the genuine hinge into direct, sustained accusation.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: creation imagery strophe: hands formed and womb's nourishment

prev_row.boundary_rationale: A fresh self-report opens the strophe: נָֽקְטָ֥ה נַפְשִׁ֗י (“My soul is weary of my life” web:Job.10.1), followed by the discourse frame אֹמַ֣ר אֶל אֱ֭לוֹהַּ (“I will tell God, 'Do not condemn me” web:Job.10.2), introducing direct second-person address to the deity that governs the rest of the strophe. Job.10.3-Job.10.7 carry that same address entirely through pronominal suffixes and verb morphology rather than any independent second-person pronoun — the 2ms independent pronoun sweeps 10 times book-wide and occurs nowhere in chapter 10 — with the interrogative particle heading three of the seven verses: “Do you have eyes of flesh? Or do you see as man sees?” web:Job.10.4, “Are your days as the days of mortals” web:Job.10.5. Job.10.6 continues the same question under כִּֽי rather than a fresh interrogative, and Job.10.7 turns concessive, “Although you know that I am not wicked” web:Job.10.7 (WEB's own rendering), closing on “there is no one who can deliver out of your hand” web:Job.10.7 before the address turns to God's creative handiwork at Job.10.8.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Stopping the strophe at Job.10.6 was rejected because Job.10.7 continues the same second-person complaint under a concessive clause (“Although you know that I am not wicked” web:Job.10.7) before the address shifts to the creation imagery opening Job.10.8, even though the interrogative particle itself does not extend past Job.10.5.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: complaint and accusation: why hide face and treat as foe

next_row.boundary_rationale: An adversative waw fronts the demonstrative object at the strophe's entry: וְ֭אֵלֶּה צָפַ֣נְתָּ בִלְבָבֶ֑ךָ (“Yet you hid these things in your heart” web:Job.10.13), pivoting from the preceding creation-gift imagery to an accusation of concealed hostile intent that runs through Job.10.17: “You renew your witnesses against me, and increase your indignation on me” web:Job.10.17. The strophe's close on “Changes and warfare are with me” web:Job.10.17 gives way to the birth-and-death lament that opens Job.10.18.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Carrying this strophe through Job.10.18 was rejected since the birth-lament question of Job.10.18 opens a distinct death-wish unit rather than continuing the renewed-witnesses accusation.
next_row.literature_type_guess: concealed hostility accusation: why reveal and then hide

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: The strophe opens still in second-person address — הַחֵ֣קֶר אֱל֣וֹהַ תִּמְצָ֑א אִ֤ם עַד תַּכְלִ֖ית שַׁדַּ֣י תִּמְצָֽא (“Can you fathom the mystery of God? Or can you probe the limits of the Almighty?” web:Job.11.7) and its parallel, גָּבְהֵ֣י שָׁ֭מַיִם מַה תִּפְעָ֑ל עֲמֻקָּ֥ה מִ֝שְּׁא֗וֹל מַה תֵּדָֽע (“...What can you do?...What can you know?” web:Job.11.8), carry four 2ms verbs between them (תִּמְצָ֑א and תִּמְצָֽא -- skeleton-tier match, distinct pointed forms; תִּפְעָ֑ל, תֵּדָֽע), continuing rather than breaking the second-person rebuke that opens this speech. The turn to third-person description is not the topic-turn interrogative itself but comes one verse later: Job.11.9's nominal clause (no expressed addressee) and, unambiguously, the 3ms protasis of Job.11.10 (אִם יַחֲלֹ֥ף וְיַסְגִּ֑יר, glossed 'if he passes by, or confines') running through Job.11.11's explicit third-person subject, כִּי ה֭וּא יָדַ֣ע מְתֵי שָׁ֑וְא (“For he knows false men” web:Job.11.11). The strophe closes on the proverb וְעַ֥יִר פֶּ֝֗רֶא אָדָ֥ם יִוָּלֵֽד (“a man is born as a wild donkey's colt” web:Job.11.12), before the address returns to second person at Job.11.13. The strophe boundary itself still rests on the topic-turn interrogative opening Job.11.7 (unsearchable-depths questions distinct from Job.11.2-Job.11.6's direct rebuke), not on a person shift that in fact arrives two verses later.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Separating Job.11.7-Job.11.8's second-person questions from Job.11.9-Job.11.12's third-person description was considered but rejected because both halves elaborate one shared claim about God's inescapable, unsearchable knowledge before the address shifts back to Job at Job.11.13.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: divine inscrutability: God's judgment deeper than earth's foundation

prev_row.boundary_rationale: Zophar's own vaya'an formula, וַ֭יַּעַן צֹפַ֥ר הַֽנַּעֲמָתִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר (Job.11.1), opens a new speech-turn, the clearest tier-1 signal available, immediately following Job's own close at Job.10.22 (petuchah, single-witness). His rebuke opens with הֲרֹ֣ב דְּ֭בָרִים לֹ֣א יֵעָנֶ֑ה (glossed ‘shouldn't the multitude of words be answered?’, Job.11.2) and continues in direct second-person address through וַ֭תֹּאמֶר זַ֣ךְ לִקְחִ֑י (“For you say, 'My doctrine is pure” web:Job.11.4). The wish מִֽי יִתֵּ֣ן אֱל֣וֹהַּ דַּבֵּ֑ר (“oh that God would speak” web:Job.11.5) continues the same second-person address into Job.11.6; this wish-clause pattern (skeleton-tier מי יתן sweep: 9 verses / 10 tokens book-wide) elsewhere carries Job's own voice, but here belongs to Zophar, and any reading of the formula as Job-exclusive must disclose this member. The strophe closes on “God exacts of you less than your iniquity deserves” web:Job.11.6 before the theological register shifts at Job.11.7.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Excluding Job.11.5-Job.11.6 from this opening strophe was rejected since the wish clause continues the same second-person rebuke begun at Job.11.2 without any intervening formula.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: Zophar opens: importunate speech and shallow wisdom rebuke

next_row.boundary_rationale: The address returns to second person at the strophe's entry, אִם אַ֭תָּ֗ה (glossed ‘if you’, Job.11.13): “If you set your heart aright, stretch out your hands toward him” web:Job.11.13. A protasis-apodosis block follows, resolving at Job.11.15 with כִּי אָ֤ז (glossed ‘surely then’): “Surely then you will lift up your face without spot” web:Job.11.15, and the promise chain continues unbroken through Job.11.19 ( “many will court your favor” web:Job.11.19 ). The closing antithesis, וְעֵינֵ֥י רְשָׁעִ֗ים (“But the eyes of the wicked will fail” web:Job.11.20), ends Zophar's speech; a petuchah follows (oshb:Job.11.20 (petuchah, single-witness)), tier-3 corroboration. Zophar's speech closes here: Job's own vaya'an formula reopens immediately at Job.12.1, the same tier-1 speaker-change spine that opened Job.9.1, marking the seam between the two speeches.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Ending this strophe at Job.11.15 was rejected because the promise clauses of Job.11.16-Job.11.19 continue the same apodosis chain that Job.11.15 opens, before the antithesis of Job.11.20 closes it.
next_row.literature_type_guess: turn and seek strophe: repentance leads to restoration

trigger_evidence.context: ֣פֶשׁ כָּל חָ֑י “in whose hand is the life of every living thing” web:Job.12.10 is a relative clause continuing v.9's th

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: A fresh imperative opens the row: וְֽאוּלָ֗ם שְׁאַל נָ֣א בְהֵמ֣וֹת וְתֹרֶ֑ךָּ “But ask the animals now, and they will teach you” web:Job.12.7. The word rendered “animals” here is the common plural of behemah (word-exact skeleton sweep: 2 book-wide, independently re-derived: 12:7 and 40:15 only), and it is a distinct homograph from the named creature at 40:15 - a general “ask the beasts” idiom here, kept separate from the later creature's count rather than blended with it. The catalog of witnesses (animals, birds, earth, fish) climaxes in the row's most disputed line: כִּ֥י יַד יְ֝הוָה עָ֣שְׂתָה זֹּֽאת “Yahweh's hand has done this” web:Job.12.9, the bare Tetragrammaton (sweep: 29 tokens / 22 verses book-wide, independently re-derived by exact word-skeleton match) appearing here as its sole occurrence inside the human dialogue - every other bare token sits in the prose frame (ch.1-2, 12 verses), the epilogue (42:7-17, 4 of its verses), or one of five remaining formula-adjacent verses in ch.38/40/42: the two storm-phrase formulas that reopen YHWH's own speeches (Job.38.1's qere מִ֥ן הַסְּעָרָ֗ה, ketiv מנ הסערה, single-witness; Job.40.6's qere מִ֥ן סְעָרָ֗ה, ketiv מנ סערה, single-witness), YHWH's second speech-opening at Job.40.1 (וַיַּ֖עַן יְהוָ֥ה אֶת אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר), and the two verses where Job's own vaya'an formula names YHWH as its object (אֶת יְהוָ֗ה) instead of opening a YHWH speech -- Job.40.3, the second of ch.40's three bare tokens, and Job.42.1 -- both reading וַיַּ֖עַן אִיּ֥וֹב אֶת יְהוָ֗ה וַיֹּאמַֽר, not a YHWH speech at all. The row continues past this anomaly without a fresh formula, vocative, or address shift: אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּ֭יָדוֹ נֶ֣פֶשׁ כָּל חָ֑י “in whose hand is the life of every living thing” web:Job.12.10 is a relative clause continuing v.9's thought, and הֲלֹא אֹ֭זֶן מִלִּ֣ין תִּבְחָ֑ן “Doesn't the ear try words” web:Job.12.11 pivots to a proverb on discernment, closing with בִּֽישִׁישִׁ֥ים חָכְמָ֑ה “With aged men is wisdom” web:Job.12.12 - answered directly by the next row's opening claim that wisdom belongs to God, not merely to age.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Carving 12:9 into its own one-verse row around the anomalous bare Yahweh token was rejected, since no formula, vocative, or discourse-frame turn isolates it from the surrounding creation-testimony catalog.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: animal instruction strophe: beasts and birds teach wisdom

prev_row.boundary_rationale: The formula וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר “Then Job answered,” web:Job.12.1 opens this row and the whole row-set: it is one of the book's eleven vaya'an tokens attributed to Job's own speaker-token (plus two vayosef tokens elsewhere, thirteen Job-attributed verse-initial formulas total, per the book's speech-formula inventory), and it immediately follows Zophar's closing gnomic warning about the wicked's “giving up of the spirit” web:Job.11.20 - a speaker change (Zophar to Job) that is the strongest available tier-1 seam. A petuchah follows 11:20 in the Masoretic tradition (oshb:Job.11.20 (petuchah, single-witness)), corroborating without driving the formula-marked opening of this speech. Job answers with direct second-person-plural address to the friends: אַתֶּם עָ֑ם “you are the people” web:Job.12.2, then לֹא נֹפֵ֣ל אָנֹכִ֣י מִכֶּ֑ם “I am not inferior to you” web:Job.12.3 (this exact four-word clause recurs, consonant-for-consonant, at 13:2 (skeleton-tier sweep: 2 book-wide; byte tier is 1 — נֹפֵ֣ל carries munach and מִכֶּ֑ם carries etnachta here, while נֹפֵ֖ל carries tipcha and מִכֶּֽם carries meteg at 13:2 — a consonantal, not byte-identical, repetition) - closing an inclusio completed at Job.13.2). At 12:4 the address drops away and Job turns to report his own case: שְׂחֹ֤ק לְרֵעֵ֨הוּ אֶֽהְיֶ֗ה “I am like one who is a joke to his neighbor” web:Job.12.4, a fronted-predicate register shift from arguing with the friends to describing his own humiliation. The strophe closes on the wicked's ease: וּֽ֭בַטֻּחוֹת לְמַרְגִּ֣יזֵי אֵ֑ל לַאֲשֶׁ֤ר הֵבִ֖יא אֱל֣וֹהַּ בְּיָדֽוֹ “Those who provoke God are secure, who carry their god in their hands” web:Job.12.6, pairing the bare divine name El with Eloah in the same line (Eloah belongs to the book's divine-name distribution, sweep: 37 tokens book-wide, confined to poetry chapters and absent from the prose frame) before the imperative that opens the next strophe.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Starting the row at 12:2 and letting 12:1's formula stand as a bare one-word seam marker on its own was rejected, since a one-clause narrative tag carries no strophe content by itself.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: Job's third response: friends address and wisdom mockery

next_row.boundary_rationale: עִ֭מּוֹ חָכְמָ֣ה וּגְבוּרָ֑ה “With God is wisdom and might” web:Job.12.13 answers the preceding proverb's claim that wisdom lies with the aged (12:12) by relocating it in God outright - a clear topic-turn from human epistemology to divine attribute. A behold-pair follows: הֵ֣ן יַ֭הֲרוֹס וְלֹ֣א יִבָּנֶ֑ה “he breaks down, and it can't be built again” web:Job.12.14, and הֵ֤ן יַעְצֹ֣ר בַּמַּ֣יִם וְיִבָ֑שׁוּ “he withholds the waters, and they dry up” web:Job.12.15. The strophe closes by repeating its own opening word: עִ֭מּוֹ עֹ֣ז וְתֽוּשִׁיָּ֑ה “With him is strength and wisdom” web:Job.12.16, an exact verse-initial refrain (sweep: 2 book-wide, exclusively at 12:13 and 12:16, independently re-derived) that brackets this thesis quatrain before the next row unpacks it into named reversals.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Running this row through 12:25 to keep the whole hymn as one span was set aside because the verse-initial refrain at 12:16 closes a self-contained thesis before the concrete catalog of reversals begins.
next_row.literature_type_guess: divine wisdom hymn: strength and counsel with God eternally

next_row.boundary_rationale: Once the inclusio bracketing Job.12.13-Job.12.16 closes on its own repeated opener (עִ֭מּוֹ, sweep: 3 book-wide; its companion pronoun ל֝֗וֹ, sweep: 4 book-wide; the two co-occur in exactly 2 verses book-wide, both at 12:13/12:16), the row opens a concrete list with no new formula or particle of its own: מוֹלִ֣יךְ יוֹעֲצִ֣ים שׁוֹלָ֑ל וְֽשֹׁפְטִ֥ים יְהוֹלֵֽל, “He leads counselors away stripped. He makes judges fools.” web:Job.12.17, continuing through kings (12:18), priests and the mighty (12:19), elders (12:20), and princes (12:21) before broadening to nations and their leaders: רָאשֵׁ֣י עַם הָאָ֑רֶץ “the chiefs of the people of the earth” web:Job.12.24. The catalog ends on a disorientation image, יְמַֽשְׁשׁוּ חֹ֥שֶׁךְ וְלֹא א֑וֹר וַ֝יַּתְעֵ֗ם כַּשִּׁכּֽוֹר “They grope in the dark without light. He makes them stagger like a drunken man.” web:Job.12.25, closing chapter 12; content, not the chapter number, drives the edge here - the wicked's would-be wisdom collapses into the same darkness the hymn opened by attributing to God alone.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 12:16 as the head of this catalog instead of the tail of the preceding thesis was considered and set aside, since the refrain word reads more naturally as closing the initial claim than opening the list of named reversals.
next_row.literature_type_guess: Hymnic catalog of God reversing counselors rulers nations

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: A bare imperative opens a new address-mode: הַחֲרִ֣ישׁוּ מִ֭מֶּנִּי וַאֲדַבְּרָה אָ֑נִי “Be silent! Leave me alone, that I may speak.” web:Job.13.13, replacing the indictment of the preceding row with a command for quiet. מָ֤ה אֶשָּׂ֣א בְשָׂרִ֣י בְשִׁנָּ֑י “take my flesh in my teeth” web:Job.13.14 carries a single-witness paseq not cited as evidence. The strophe's crux is textual: at 13:15 the OSHB extract carries a ketiv/qere pair immediately adjacent, לא (ketiv) beside ל֣וֹ (qere, single-witness); the WEB rendering quoted here, הֵ֣ן יִ֭קְטְלֵנִי לא ל֣וֹ אֲיַחֵ֑ל “he will kill me. I have no hope.” web:Job.13.15, follows the ketiv reading, while the qere tradition points to a different sense - both are disclosed here without adjudicating between them. The row closes on a legal rhetorical question, מִי ה֭וּא יָרִ֣יב עִמָּדִ֑י “Who is he who will contend with me?” web:Job.13.19, still referring to God in the third person rather than addressing him directly, which is exactly what changes at the next row's opening particle.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this resolve into the preceding indictment was rejected, since the imperative here commands silence rather than continuing to name the friends' faults.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: Resolve declaration with silence command fronted

prev_row.boundary_rationale: A presentative particle reopens direct address to the friends: הֶן כֹּ֭ל רָאֲתָ֣ה עֵינִ֑י, “Behold, my eye has seen all this.” web:Job.13.1, and לֹא נֹפֵ֖ל אָנֹכִ֣י מִכֶּֽם, “I am not inferior to you.” web:Job.13.2, repeats the same four-word clause Job already used at Job.12.3 — consonant-identical (skeleton-tier sweep: 2 book-wide) though not byte-identical (נֹפֵ֣ל carries munach and מִכֶּ֑ם carries etnachta at Job.12.3; נֹפֵ֖ל carries tipcha and מִכֶּֽם carries meteg at Job.13.2), and verse-final only here: at Job.12.3 the same clause sits mid-verse, followed by a third colon (“Yes, who doesn't know such things as these?” web:Job.12.3). The repetition still returns the speech to the friends-address register before it pivots away again. That pivot comes at once: אוּלָ֗ם אֲ֭נִי אֶל שַׁדַּ֣י אֲדַבֵּ֑ר וְהוֹכֵ֖חַ אֶל אֵ֣ל אֶחְפָּֽץ, rendered “I would speak to the Almighty. I desire to reason with God.” web:Job.13.3, a bicolon in which the bare consonant string אֶל appears twice as its own preposition ('to') — once governing שַׁדַּ֣י ('Shaddai') in one colon, once governing אֵ֣ל ('El', the divine name itself) in the other — parallel clauses rather than one slot holding both names in apposition (a homograph the row does not blend into any count). The indictment proper follows: וְֽאוּלָ֗ם אַתֶּ֥ם טֹֽפְלֵי שָׁ֑קֶר רֹפְאֵ֖י אֱלִ֣ל כֻּלְּכֶֽם “you are forgers of lies. You are all physicians of no value.” web:Job.13.4, including the wish מִֽי יִ֭תֵּן הַחֲרֵ֣שׁ תַּחֲרִישׁ֑וּן “Oh that you would be completely silent!” web:Job.13.5 (one of ten book-wide mi-yitten tokens, independently re-derived, kept here as texture rather than a fresh boundary since nothing else turns at this line), an imperative to reason together at 13:6, and the charge of partiality through 13:11, closing on זִֽ֭כְרֹנֵיכֶם מִשְׁלֵי אֵ֑פֶר “Your memorable sayings are proverbs of ashes” web:Job.13.12 before the row's own imperative shift into silence at 13:13.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting off 13:5-12 on the strength of the mi-yitten wish at 13:5 or the imperative at 13:6 was rejected, since the whole span stays one continuous second-person indictment, closed by the ashes-and-clay image at 13:12 alone.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: Job's claim of parity with friend-indictment formulation

next_row.boundary_rationale: A restrictive particle opens direct second-person-singular address to God, unattested earlier in this speech: אַךְ שְׁ֭תַּיִם אַל תַּ֣עַשׂ עִמָּדִ֑י “Only don't do two things to me” web:Job.13.20, immediately specified as כַּ֭פְּךָ מֵעָלַ֣י הַרְחַ֑ק “withdraw your hand far from me” web:Job.13.21. This address shift - from the friends, or from soliloquy about God in the third person, to God as direct addressee - is the strongest interior seam in this speech. The petition turns accusatory, לָֽמָּה פָנֶ֥יךָ תַסְתִּ֑יר וְתַחְשְׁבֵ֖נִי לְאוֹיֵ֣ב לָֽךְ “Why do you hide your face, and consider me your enemy?” web:Job.13.24, and lands in legal complaint: וְתָ֘שֵׂ֤ם בַּסַּ֨ד רַגְלַ֗י וְתִשְׁמ֥וֹר כָּל אָרְחוֹתָ֑י “You also put my feet in the stocks, and mark all my paths.” web:Job.13.27 (single-witness paseq, not cited as evidence), closing the chapter on וְ֭הוּא כְּרָקָ֣ב יִבְלֶ֑ה כְּ֝בֶ֗גֶד “I am decaying like a rotten thing” web:Job.13.28. Job.13.28 itself already opens with an explicit third-person subject, וְ֭הוּא ('and he/it', continuing the moth-eaten-garment simile), rather than the second-person address to God that carries Job.13.20-Job.13.27; this row keeps Job.13.28 on its own side of the seam because the addressee (God, second person) still governs the verse's surrounding argument and no fresh discourse frame or vocative opens elsewhere, but the person shift is a genuine crux at the row's own far edge, disclosed rather than smoothed into an unbroken second-person run. The following row's fresh universal subject, 'man' in general rather than Job's own case, opens at Job.14.1.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row through 14:6 to keep the entire divine-address arc in one span was considered and set aside, since a fresh universal subject opens chapter 14 as its own meditation rather than continuing the personal two-requests petition.
next_row.literature_type_guess: Direct petition syntax with covenant-suit complaint

next_row.boundary_rationale: A fresh universal subject opens the row: אָ֭דָם יְל֣וּד אִשָּׁ֑ה קְצַ֥ר יָ֝מִ֗ים “Man, who is born of a woman, is of few days” web:Job.14.1, followed by כְּצִ֣יץ יָ֭צָא וַיִּמָּ֑ל “He grows up like a flower, and is cut down” web:Job.14.2, both third-person. The second-person address to God carried over from the preceding row resurfaces mid-strophe: וְאֹ֘תִ֤י תָבִ֖יא בְמִשְׁפָּ֣ט עִמָּֽךְ “bring me into judgment with you” web:Job.14.3, and מִֽי יִתֵּ֣ן טָ֭הוֹר מִטָּמֵ֗א “Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean?” web:Job.14.4 (another of the ten book-wide mi-yitten tokens, texture here, not a fresh boundary). At 14:5 the OSHB extract carries a ketiv/qere pair adjacent, חקו (ketiv) beside חֻקָּ֥יו (qere, single-witness); Job.14.5 also carries a single-witness paseq elsewhere in the verse (inventory count alone, no word-level position encoded); the row quotes חֻקָּ֥יו עָ֝שִׂ֗יתָ וְלֹ֣א יַעֲבֽוֹר “you have appointed his bounds that he can't pass” web:Job.14.5. It closes with an imperative petition, שְׁעֵ֣ה מֵעָלָ֣יו וְיֶחְדָּ֑ל “Look away from him, that he may rest” web:Job.14.6, before an explanatory particle opens a fresh analogy in the next row.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting off 14:3-6's direct address from 14:1-2's third-person description was rejected, since the whole row stays one meditation that simply moves between describing man and petitioning God about him, with no formula or vocative marking a fresh start.
